Modern.brandNameRationale: Single word. Session is what therapy is, said as plainly as the customer would say it. The brand puts the basic unit of the work in the brand position. Modern, direct, low-friction. No clinical jargon. No metaphor.
Modern.industrySummary: Mental health has gone mainstream. The customer base is larger and more design-literate than ever, and they have less tolerance for the cold clinical aesthetic the category traditionally used. Modern players are competing on warmth, accessibility, and brand quality.
Modern.competitorLandscape: BetterHelp (betterhelp.com) holds the volume D2C tier. Talkspace (talkspace.com) is the institutional peer. Alma (helloalma.com) does the design-led therapist marketplace. Two Chairs (twochairs.com) sits in the in-network premium tier. We sit closest to Alma in tone.
Modern.positioningStatement: Therapy booking that works the way modern services should: clear pricing, clear matching, clear next steps.

targetAudience.primary: 25 to 45. Has thought about therapy for years and never started. Wants the booking to feel like a service, not a leap. Will pay out of pocket for the right match.

dos: Show the therapist's actual photo and bio
Confirm the booking in one short message
donts: Photograph models pretending to be in therapy

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark only. SESSION in a soft modern grotesk, slightly humanist, all caps with wide kerning. A small horizontal pulse mark beneath the wordmark, suggesting calm rhythm. Used as the app icon and on the appointment card.

colorPalette.name: Session Navy
colorPalette.meaning: Trust, calm, the deep end of a soft pool.

colorPalette.name: Cream
colorPalette.meaning: Used as space. The waiting room.

typography.rationale: Inter handles the booking and product surfaces, where clarity is the priority. The grotesk carries the warmer brand surface.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No 'mental wellness journey' content. No streaks. No anxiety quizzes used as marketing. No celebrity therapy ambassadors.

customSections.title: Where it lives
customSections.body: An app that books in three taps. Therapist matches based on actual conversation, not a 30-question form. Sessions confirmed by SMS. A single annual email with the practice news. No push notifications.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Two words. Linwood sounds like a real place or a quiet street. Counsel is the older word for the therapeutic relationship, before 'therapy' became a category. The pair reads as a small, established practice serving a specific kind of client over many years.
Luxury.story: Linwood Counsel was founded by a small group of psychotherapists who had spent decades inside larger institutional practices and wanted to take fewer clients, more carefully. The practice accepts a limited number of patients each year. Some have been with the practice since it opened.
Luxury.industrySummary: Top end psychotherapy has been moving toward concierge services bolted onto larger systems. There's a parallel market for small, principal-led practices in the older tradition. Few patients, long engagements, decades-long relationships. The customer is paying for the therapist, the practice, and the next hour.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Brick (brickbymanhattan.com) sits in the premium psychotherapy tier. The Practice (similar private practices in Mayfair, the Upper East Side, Pacific Heights) are the peers. We sit closer to a Harley Street consulting room than to any digital-first peer.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A small psychotherapy practice for clients who treat the work as central, not optional.

targetAudience.primary: 40 and up. High-functioning. Often has tried therapy before and wants something deeper. Pays out of pocket. Values the long relationship with the therapist over the convenience of the booking flow.

dos: Address the client by surname or chosen name
Speak in the language of the discipline
Send paper letters where the situation warrants

Luxury.logoDirection: A classical serif wordmark with elegant ligatures. A small hand-drawn ampersand-like flourish becomes the practice's hallmark, used on letterhead, the brass plaque outside the practice, and the wax seal of every paper letter.

colorPalette.name: Counsel Green
colorPalette.meaning: Old leather, library walls, the practice's waiting room.

typography.primary: Canela for the wordmark and printed material
typography.secondary: Söhne for the secure client portal
typography.rationale: A high contrast classical serif sets the heritage tone. A modern grotesk handles the few digital surfaces. Both restrained.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No insurance billing. No therapist directory listings. No content marketing. No press. No social media presence.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Single word. Talk is what therapy actually is, stripped of clinical language. The brand puts the act in the brand position. Plain. Specific. Unpretentious.
Minimal.industrySummary: Mental health brands have been adding features for years (chatbots, mood trackers, meditation libraries, sleep stories). There's an opening for one that subtracts. One thing. Talking to a person.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Most modern mental health apps compete on what they include. We compete on absence. The closest peer in spirit is Open Path Collective (openpathcollective.org) on the affordability side, with a sharper minimal aesthetic.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A therapy practice with one offering: sessions with a therapist. No app extras.

targetAudience.primary: Adults who want therapy and don't want a mental health app. They want to book, attend, and continue. No streaks, no journals, no AI.

dos: Show the session length and price
Confirm the booking in one line

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark only. TALK in a single weight grotesk, wide kerned, all caps, four letters with generous space. No icon. The app, the website, and the appointment card all carry the wordmark and nothing else.

typography.rationale: One face. The app is the wordmark, the appointment, the therapist's name. Nothing else.

customSections.title: Not this
customSections.body: No mood tracker. No journal feature. No meditation library. No AI chatbot. No streaks. No notifications.

Corporate.tagline: Behavioral health services for the enterprise.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Three words. Threshold suggests the point of change. Behavioral Health is the buyer-side word for the category. The whole name reads like a real, established clinical-services firm already on the panel of every major health plan and self-insured employer.
Corporate.industrySummary: Enterprise behavioral health is a serious B2B category. Self-insured employers, health plans, and integrated health systems need partners who can deliver behavioral health programs at scale with clinical rigor and regulatory-grade reporting.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Lyra Health (lyrahealth.com) is the modern enterprise leader. Spring Health (springhealth.com) sits closely. Modern Health (joinmodernhealth.com) is the peer. Beacon Health Options (now part of Carelon) holds the institutional position. We sit closer to Lyra in posture, with stronger clinical-network focus.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Behavioral health programs for self-insured employers and integrated health systems.
Corporate.positioningRationale: Employers and health systems want clinical partners they can trust to deliver outcomes, not just enrollments. We position on the clinical depth of the network and the reporting discipline of the operations.

targetAudience.primary: Chief Medical Officers, VPs of Benefits, and Population Health Directors at self-insured employers and integrated health systems with at least 5000 covered lives.
motivations: Clinical network depth that holds up under utilization
Outcome reporting that satisfies regulators and CFOs
One partner across EAP, in-network therapy, and crisis support

dos: Speak to the buyer, not the patient

messagingPillars.name: Clinical network depth
messagingPillars.description: Therapists, psychiatrists, and care navigators in network across every geography the buyer covers.

messagingPillars.name: Outcomes-grade reporting
messagingPillars.description: PHQ-9, GAD-7, and other validated outcome measures reported at the cohort level, formatted for the CMO and CFO.

messagingPillars.name: Full continuum of care
messagingPillars.description: EAP, outpatient therapy, psychiatry, and crisis support under one contract.

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small geometric mark to the left. The mark is a single open doorway silhouette, reduced to three lines. Reads cleanly on a procurement deck, name badge, and patient-facing card.

typography.primary: Inter for marketing and product UI
typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for printed clinical literature
typography.rationale: Inter scales clean across digital. The serif handles formal clinical reports and trust center documentation.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No D2C app. No retail clinics. No influencer therapists. The firm sells through enterprise procurement, not Instagram mental health content.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Two words. Good Days names what the customer actually wants from the work. Not 'wellness' or 'thriving' or 'transformation'. Just more good days than bad. Honest, warm, and grounded.
Creative.manifesto: Most mental health brands sound like a textbook trying to be soft. They moralize. They over-promise. They use words nobody says out loud. Good Days is the brand for therapy that sounds like a real conversation. The work is serious. The voice doesn't have to be.
Creative.industrySummary: Mental health branding has been earnest, cool-toned, and slightly preachy. There's room for one that's warm, character-driven, and still serious about the actual clinical work.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Real (joinreal.com) does playful well in clinical adjacent spaces. Mindful (mindful.org) holds the older mindfulness content. Headspace (headspace.com) does the mass meditation tier. We sit warmer than all of them, with a clearer point of view.
Creative.positioningStatement: A therapy and mental health brand that sounds like a real friend, not a textbook.

targetAudience.primary: 25 to 45. Has been to therapy or wants to go. Already familiar with mental health language and slightly exhausted by it. Wants a brand that talks like they do.

dos: Use real language people use about their feelings
Tell the truth about what therapy is and isn't
donts: Photograph models in white linen at sunset

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark in a punchy display serif with the O of GOOD stylized as a small open circle, suggesting a sun rising or a thought bubble. Standalone open-circle icon for app icons, stickers, and social profiles. The mark reads warm at every size.

colorPalette.name: Day Yellow
colorPalette.usage: Primary brand color, hero surfaces, social

typography.primary: Migra for the wordmark and big display
typography.secondary: PP Neue Montreal for body and signage
typography.rationale: Migra has warmth and character. Neue Montreal keeps the practical bits readable. The pair feels designed and human.

customSections.title: What it isn't
customSections.body: Not a meditation app. Not a transformation brand. Not afraid of yellow. Not too cool to make a joke about therapy.

customSections.title: Where it lives
customSections.body: An app that opens to a single warm message. A printed mood journal that's actually beautiful, sold separately. A weekly newsletter written like a friend checking in. Stickers in every welcome envelope.
